sections.skill: Compare fixed-rate and adjustable-rate mortgages and budget for the full cost of owning a home

questions.prompt: Which statement describes a FIXED-rate mortgage?

choices.text: The rate changes every single year with the overall market
The payment changes when the Fed changes rates
The interest rate stays the same for the whole loan
Payments rise every month by law

questions.correct_answer: The interest rate stays the same for the whole loan
questions.intro: A fixed-rate mortgage keeps the same interest rate (and principal-and-interest payment) for the whole loan. An adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) has a fixed rate for an initial period (for example, 5 years in a "5/1" ARM) and then adjusts periodically based on a market index plus a margin, within limits called caps.
questions.feedback: Fixed-rate means the rate never changes.
questions.topic: Fixed or adjustable rates, and the true cost of owning

misconceptions.A: Describes an ARM after its fixed period

sources: CFPB (Adjustable-rate mortgages): An ARM has an initial fixed period, after which the rate adjusts based on an index plus a margin, subject to caps. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-an-adjustable-rate-mortgage-arm-en-100/)

questions.prompt: A 5/1 ARM starts at 5.5% on $240,000, with a $1,362.69 payment. After 5 years, the balance is $221,905.45 and the rate rises to 7.5%; the new payment is $1,639.86. How much does the payment rise?
questions.intro: An ARM's payment can rise when its rate resets. Plan for the possible higher payment, not only the starting one.

A buyer on a tight budget who plans to stay 30 years

questions.correct_answer: A buyer who expects to sell before the fixed period ends
